title: What Is TypeScript?
summary: TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript whose types are checked at compile time and then erased. Learn what the compiler does, what structural typing means, and where TypeScript 7's native compiler fits.

title: Setting Up TypeScript
summary: Install TypeScript, compile with tsc, use the Playground, and create your first tsconfig.json — including what turning on strict actually does.

title: Basic Types
summary: The primitive types, arrays, null and undefined, the difference between any and unknown, and how TypeScript infers a type when you don't annotate one.

title: Functions and Inference
summary: Type function parameters and return values, use optional, default, and rest parameters, understand void, and see how contextual typing infers types for you.

title: Objects and Interfaces
summary: Describe the shape of objects with object types and interfaces: optional and readonly properties, index signatures, and excess-property checks.

title: Union and Literal Types
summary: Model a value that can be one of several types with unions, restrict it to exact values with literal types, understand literal widening, and narrow with typeof.

title: Type Aliases, Arrays, and Tuples
summary: Name types with type aliases and know when to prefer them over interfaces; type arrays; and use tuples, readonly tuples, and named tuple members.

title: Narrowing and Type Guards
summary: Teach the compiler which type a value has right now using typeof, instanceof, in, truthiness, discriminated unions, and your own type-guard functions.

title: Generics
summary: Write functions, interfaces, and classes that work over many types without losing type safety: type parameters, constraints with extends, and default type parameters.

title: Classes
summary: Type classes in TypeScript: fields and methods, the public/private/protected modifiers, readonly, parameter properties, JavaScript #private fields, abstract classes, and implements.

title: Enums and const Assertions
summary: How numeric and string enums behave at runtime, the const enum caveat, the as const assertion, and when a union of literals is the better choice.

title: Advanced Function Types
summary: Overload signatures, typing this in functions, assertion functions, and applying generic constraints to functions.

title: unknown, never, and Type Assertions
summary: The safe top type unknown, the bottom type never and exhaustiveness checks, type assertions with as, the non-null assertion, and the satisfies operator.

title: Modules and Declaration Files
summary: ES module import/export, import type, ambient declarations and .d.ts files, the @types ecosystem, and how module resolution finds your imports.

title: The tsconfig Options That Matter
summary: The compiler options you actually reach for: the strict family, target, module and moduleResolution, esModuleInterop, isolatedModules, noEmit, and project references.

title: Utility Types
summary: The built-in type transformers: Partial, Required, Readonly, Pick, Omit, Record, Exclude, Extract, NonNullable, ReturnType, Parameters, and Awaited.

title: keyof, typeof, and Indexed Access Types
summary: Query types instead of writing them by hand: the keyof operator, the typeof type query, and indexed access types like T[K].

title: Conditional Types
summary: Choose a type based on a condition with T extends U ? X : Y, understand how conditionals distribute over unions, and extract types with infer.

title: Mapped Types
summary: Build a new object type from an existing one by mapping over its keys, remapping keys with as, and adding or removing the readonly and optional modifiers.

title: Template Literal Types
summary: Compute string literal types with template literal syntax, combine unions inside a template, and use the intrinsic Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize, and Uncapitalize types.

title: Generics in Depth
summary: Go deeper into generics: an intuition for variance, higher-order type inference, const type parameters, and practical constraint and default patterns.

title: Declaration Merging and Module Augmentation
summary: How TypeScript merges multiple declarations of the same name, augmenting third-party modules, extending global types with declare global, and where namespaces still fit.

title: Decorators
summary: The standard ECMAScript decorators supported since TypeScript 5.0 for classes, methods, accessors, and fields — plus a note on the legacy experimentalDecorators.

title: Typing Async Code and Migrating JavaScript
summary: Type Promises and async/await, write a typed fetch, handle unknown errors in catch, and migrate an existing JavaScript codebase to TypeScript step by step.
